title: Ergodicity of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
main_claim: For every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle that is an irrational multiple of pi, the billiard flow is ergodic for normalized Liouville measure. The core result is Proposition (prop:rigidity): every bounded geodesic-invariant function on the flat double has parallel angular Fourier coefficients. The irrational cone angle's holonomy then forces the function to be constant.

issues.location: Section 5, Proposition prop:rigidity (main.tex ~l.430-650); also Lemma lem:bounded-modes
issues.description: This is not a demonstrated gap; I am flagging it so an expert checks it. The analytic Proposition never uses irrationality. It applies to every compact flat cone surface, including translation surfaces, where it gives that almost every direction is ergodic (Kerckhoff-Masur-Smillie). That would be a new elementary proof of KMS that avoids Teichmueller dynamics. Together with the holonomy step it would also settle the open question of whether every flat cone surface with an irrational cone angle is ergodic. I checked each step and found no failure: the CR norm identity via Stokes, the telescoping energy bound, the cone-annulus cutoff bound, XU=B, the bad-set measure O(s), ||Xg||<=2H/T, the adjoint identity and both weak-limit identifications. Given how strong the claim is, an independent specialist should verify it, especially Lemma lem:bounded-modes. That lemma gives an H^1 bound on each mode of every L^infinity invariant function, and it is the step that replaces Forni-Moll's H^{1,0} hypothesis.
issues.evidence: 'Throughout the analytic argument, the triangle is fixed and nondegenerate; no irrationality assumption is needed until Section conclusion.' / Lemma lem:bounded-modes: '||nabla h_j||_2 <= CH (j in Z)' for any bounded h with Xh=0.
